failures.rule: brand/constitution.md, Article 7.6, Part III App canvas, B28
failures.place: All three phone frames on each board
failures.issue: The board has no 390 × 844 pt true-scale anchor. The left and right frames are about 485 × 1024 pixels, which become roughly 390 × 824 when scaled to the required width; the middle frame is narrower. These are not consistently proportioned 390 × 844 screens, so the depicted thumb reach and spacing cannot be accepted as true-scale evidence.

failures.rule: brand/ledger.md, Decided A3 and Open D6; brand/constitution.md, Article 6 roles and B14; product/ui-constitution.md, Article 7
failures.place: Wordmark, item title, button labels and $31.40 in the Sold and Shipping panels
failures.issue: The type roles do not hold at phone scale. Relative to a 390-wide screen, the wordmark appears about 26 rather than 21, and the item title and button labels about 19 rather than 15. Conversely, the peak amount appears about 40 rather than the 50 required by every D6 option. These are visual estimates from the raster, not computed font sizes; the relative scale mismatch is visible across all three options.

across_options.issue: opt-B omits the lower arrow segment from Accept $38 into the offer-to-Sold transition. A and C connect the primary action to the transition; B leaves the upper curve starting at the offer card. This changes the experience annotation independently of D6 (brand/constitution.md Article 14.4: variants differ on one named axis).

The offer field is not held constant: its texture contrast and line pattern differ, with C visibly fainter than A/B; B also has a slightly wider offer card. These are field and geometry variations, not changes to the sale amount (brand/ledger.md D5 versus D6; brand/constitution.md Article 14.4).

Sold and Shipping fills vary slightly between renders in addition to their shared palette drift. The thumb arc, transition curves and small text/edge placements also shift slightly. The comparisons are therefore not pixel-stable outside D6; minor raster differences are less consequential than B’s missing action arrow.
